title: Camera3R: Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Heterogeneous Camera Models
claim: One feed-forward model turns mixed, unknown input views into accurate scene reconstructions that closely match ground truth.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right, 2 scene rows, input to reconstruction to ground truth
description: A three-column gallery with a bold header over each column: Input (Mixed Cameras), Reconstruction, and Ground Truth. The top row is an outdoor street scene. The inputs are one perspective image and two circular fisheye images, and the reconstruction and ground truth are colored point clouds seen from above. The bottom row is an indoor office scene. The inputs are a panoramic or wide-angle view, a distorted wide-angle view and two perspective views, shown as a 2x2 grid. The reconstruction and ground-truth point clouds are rendered from above. The reconstruction column sits next to the ground-truth column, so a reader can compare them directly. There are no arrows or diagrams. The eye goes first to the colorful fisheye photos and then to the dense point clouds. The reconstructions resemble the ground truth, and the indoor one is very close.
caption: \paragraphtitle{3D reconstruction from heterogeneous cameras.} Given an image sequence of arbitrary, unknown, and mixed camera models, our method reconstructs the scene in a single forward pass.
abstract: Feed-forward 3D reconstruction (3R) from unconstrained multi-view images has recently emerged as a prominent research direction in 3D computer vision. Various foundational reconstruction models have been proposed with different architectures and reconstruction paradigms. Despite being trained on large-scale perspective datasets with substantial computational resources, these models generally struggle to generalize to non-perspective images. This limitation hinders their deployment in applications involving arbitrary, unknown, and potentially heterogeneous camera models. To build on the capabilities of existing reconstruction models with minimal retraining, we propose Camera3R, a low-rank adaptation framework that efficiently extends perspective-pretrained 3R networks to any other camera models. Extensive experiments demonstrate that, with only 0.5% additional parameters and less than a day of training, Camera3R adapts a foundational 3D reconstruction model to non-perspective cameras while fully preserving its original performance on perspective inputs. Code is available at https://github.com/android-xr/camera3r.
